rows.evidence: Q1: Material and methods - two-season (2014-2015) mini-lysimeter experiment with DI and SDI treatments on forage corn at Karaj, Iran. Q2: Table 4 and Results - WUE of corn was 8.32 kg/m3 under SDI versus 6.67 under DI (mean of two seasons), with SDI significantly higher in both years. Q4: Table 2 and Results - the study measured the intermediate variables: seasonal soil evaporation was lower under SDI (157.6 mm) than DI (197.9 mm) and transpiration higher under SDI, with ETc-act lower under SDI (384.8 vs 423.4 mm), which is the mechanism given for the higher WUE.
rows.notes: Single method (water-balance mini-lysimeters, E from unplanted mini-lysimeters, WUE = biomass/ETc-act), so no triangulation. Single loamy soil, one crop, one site; mini-lysimeter (plot) scale only. No conditions stated as requirements for the WUE advantage (burial depth of 30 cm is a design choice, not stated as a requirement). No explicit limitations of the WUE result; the only caveat mentioned (ETo overestimation by FAO-PM) concerns the Kcb comparison. Only LSD letter groupings, no SD/CI/range reported.

rows.evidence: Q1: Material and methods - own two-season mini-lysimeter experiment comparing DI and SDI on corn.
rows.notes: The study does not measure or report weed occurrence anywhere in the methods, results or tables. The only mention is an assertion in the abstract's Research highlights that SDI superiority 'contributed to ... low weed incidence', with no data behind it. The study's own results concern ETc-act, E, Tp, crop coefficients, LAI, height, stem diameter, biomass and WUE. Hence no own evidence on the weed-reduction effect claimed in the passage.

rows.evidence: Q1: Material and methods - two-season mini-lysimeter experiment with three replicates each of DI and SDI on forage corn. Q2: Table 4 and Results - biomass yield was 81.90 ton/ha under SDI versus 63.21 ton/ha under DI (mean), significantly higher under SDI in both 2014 and 2015. Q4: Table 2 and Table 4 - the study measured intermediate variables through which SDI raises biomass: higher plant transpiration (250.1 vs 221.8 mm), lower soil evaporation, and higher LAI (4.6 vs 3.4), plant height and stem diameter under SDI.
rows.notes: Yield measured by one method (harvested biomass in mini-lysimeters); no triangulation. Single site, soil and crop; mini-lysimeter scale. The explanation that optimal root-zone moisture favoured uptake is asserted with citations rather than measured as soil moisture, but the measured Tp/E/LAI partition counts as the intermediate variable. No requirements for the effect stated from own findings, no limitations stated, and no dispersion measures (letter groupings only).

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a single-site, two-year mini-lysimeter comparison of surface vs subsurface drip on forage corn in Karaj, Iran; results given as means with LSD letter groupings only. Weed incidence is mentioned only in the abstract highlights without any supporting data.
